svg.title: The Vulkan compute path in fak: Go backend, cgo boundary, the libfakvulkan C shim, SPIR-V shaders, and the Vulkan driver, with the per-dispatch tax marked at each crossing
svg.desc: A vertical stack of five layers. At the top, the Go forward loop calls whole operations on the compute.Backend interface. Below it, internal/compute/vulkan.go is the Go backend, built only under the tag vulkan and cgo (internal/compute/vulkan.go:1), which registers itself at internal/compute/vulkan.go:214 from its init at internal/compute/vulkan.go:171 and declares correctness class Approx at internal/compute/vulkan.go:587. A single mutex, vulkanMu at internal/compute/vulkan.go:69, serializes the whole backend, so only one operation is in flight at a time. The cgo boundary crosses into the C++ shim internal/compute/vulkan_shim.cpp, 9157 lines, which exposes a flat C ABI of fvk_ functions: fvk_init at internal/compute/vulkan_shim.cpp:3326, fvk_device_identity at internal/compute/vulkan_shim.cpp:3279, fvk_free at internal/compute/vulkan_shim.cpp:118. The shim is compiled offline into a static library named libfakvulkan.a. Below the shim, 116 SPIR-V compute shaders in internal/compute/shaders/ carry the actual arithmetic, for example matmul.comp, attention.comp and q4k_matmul.comp. At the bottom, the Vulkan driver and the GPU. The per-dispatch tax is marked at each crossing: every small operation pays a Go-to-C call, a command-buffer record, a queue submit and a fence wait, which is why the backend is numerically correct but roughly 60 times slower than llama.cpp.
svg.text: The Vulkan compute path — five layers, and where the time goes
Vulkan is a graphics API pressed into compute service. It works on every vendor, and it charges a toll at every crossing.
1 · the forward loop — calls whole operations, never names a backend
MatMul · BatchedMatMul · Attention · Argmax — the compute.Backend interface, internal/compute/compute.go:450
2 · internal/compute/vulkan.go — the Go backend
//go:build vulkan && (windows || linux) && cgo — a default go build ./... skips this file entirely
init() at vulkan.go:171 → Register(vulkanDev) at vulkan.go:214 · Class() = Approx at vulkan.go:587
vulkanMu (vulkan.go:69) — ONE mutex serializes the whole backend: one operation in flight, ever
◀ crossing 1: cgo call (Go → C)
3 · internal/compute/vulkan_shim.cpp — the C++ shim (9,157 lines)
a flat C ABI of fvk_ functions — fvk_init (vulkan_shim.cpp:3326) · fvk_device_identity (:3279) · fvk_free (:118)
compiled OFFLINE into a static library: libfakvulkan.a — the same libfak<backend>.a convention as libfakcuda.a
here the shim records a command buffer, submits it to a queue, and waits on a fence — per operation
◀ crossing 2: vkQueueSubmit + fence wait
4 · internal/compute/shaders/ — 116 SPIR-V compute shaders
the actual arithmetic lives here, not in Go: matmul.comp · attention.comp · q4k_matmul.comp · argmax.comp
SPIR-V is Vulkan's portable bytecode — one binary the driver translates to whatever the card speaks
descriptor sets bind the buffers; the driver validates and compiles the pipeline
5 · the Vulkan driver and the GPU
witnessed on an AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RDNA3 / gfx1102, 8 GB) — argmax-exact, prefill-logit cosine = 1.0
The per-dispatch tax: a transformer forward pass is thousands of SMALL operations. Each one pays crossings 1 and 2 in full.
The GPU finishes the arithmetic long before the CPU finishes handing it over — hence correct, but ~60× slower than llama.cpp.
